title: $331 Million to a Dictator's Daughter: The Telia Uzbekistan Ledger
title_options: $331 Million to a Dictator's Daughter: The Telia Uzbekistan Ledger
How Sweden's State Telecom Bribed Its Way Into Uzbekistan and Paid $965 Million to Washington
Telia and Gulnara Karimova: The Bribe Sweden Could Not Prosecute
The Swedish State Owned 37% of Telia. It Still Paid a Dictator's Daughter $331 Million.
$965 Million, Zero Convictions: The TeliaSonera Uzbekistan Affair, Audited
description:
In 2007 TeliaSonera, Sweden's former telephone monopoly and still 37 percent owned by the Swedish state, entered Uzbekistan by paying a Gibraltar shell company run by a 24-year-old assistant to Gulnara Karimova, the president's daughter. Over the next three years the payments reached about $331 million. A Swedish television programme exposed it in September 2012. The chief executive resigned in February 2013. In September 2017 Telia paid $965 million to the United States and the Netherlands, the third-largest foreign-bribery settlement ever at the time. Sweden charged three former executives and lost, twice. This is the Telia Uzbekistan ledger: Takilant, Uppdrag granskning, Lars Nyberg, the deferred prosecution agreement, VimpelCom and MTS, the Stockholm acquittals, Karimova's prison sentence, and why the money went to Washington and The Hague, not Stockholm.
